planting.note: Plant bulbs with the neck at or just below the soil surface in moist to boggy, fertile soil in full sun to light shade; this old Southern garden hybrid tolerates wetter, heavier soil than most Hymenocallis and multiplies readily into dense clumps.

directions: Despite the name, this is one of the most cold-hardy and reliable spider lilies for Gulf Coast gardens, surviving in old abandoned homesites across the Deep South for generations. Set bulbs in rich, consistently moist to boggy soil near a pond edge, rain garden, or low spot in full sun to light shade. Clumps expand steadily from offsets and need little division; established plantings bloom reliably in mid to late summer with fragrant, pure white, spidery flowers held well above the glossy, strap-shaped foliage. Mulch is rarely needed for winter protection within its hardiness range, but a hard freeze may kill foliage back without harming the bulb.
